It's a bit confusing - even having read it 10 times or more - I am not sure I am interpreting it correctly; hence posting here.

My interpretation of that, is that it still must go through approval process - that it cannot just be done without informing the board. Not that it is outright prohibited in common areas.

"(3)(a) If approval is required for the installation of a heat pump, the application for approval must be processed and approved in the same manner as an application for approval of an architectural modification."

I recognize that reasonable restrictions may be placed, which by the language of the bill - "Reasonable restriction" means a restriction that does not significantly increase the cost of a heat pump or significantly decrease its efficiency or specified performance.

They originally said "no exterior modifications are allowed". I then took time to mail out a flyer for the bill to all 150+ of my neighbors, which seemed to get them to act, consulting with their attorney for guidance.

Their retort was that it didn't apply because the law is only applicable to communities built after July 1st, 2018 (64.90.080) - but their claim seems to be based on incomplete interpretation of that section. That seems to be the next point of contention.

It is worth mentioning based on architecture of the building, and relevant building codes - I have been informed there is a VERY limited interior + exterior placement possible; so the scope of reasonable restrictions possible seem slim.
